You are reviewing Task 2 of a 9-task visual redesign of a static vanilla-JS website. Review for SPEC COMPLIANCE and TASK QUALITY. Both verdicts are required.

Working directory: c:\Users\leont\Desktop\CleaningSystem-main

Read these three files:
1. Requirements (the brief): .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-28-cleaning-site-redesign/task-2-brief.md
2. Implementer's report: .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-28-cleaning-site-redesign/task-2-report.md
3. The diff under review: .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-28-cleaning-site-redesign/review-4137c07..31309ad.diff

GLOBAL CONSTRAINTS that bind this task — copied verbatim from the plan. These are your attention lens:
1. No content text changes. Not one character of any user-facing string in any of the 7 locales (ru, en, fr, it, es, de, nl). Translation objects are read-only. Every `${t.…}` expression must be byte-identical; all seven <option> lines in the language selector must be byte-identical.
2. No structural changes. No elements added, removed, or re-nested. The ONLY permitted attribute edits in this task are: removing style="…" and adding class="…".
3. `frontend/` is a stale duplicate tree — must not be read from or written to.
4. THREE inline styles MUST BE PRESERVED because JS mutates them at runtime. Removing any breaks the before/after comparison slider:
   - js/pages/portfolio.js — style="display: none;" on #portfolio-modal (set to 'flex' on card click)
   - js/pages/portfolio.js — style="width: 50%;" on .before-img (set by updateSlider)
   - js/pages/portfolio.js — style="left: 50%;" on .slider-handle (set by updateSlider)
   These three must be the ONLY style= attributes remaining in the whole project.
5. This task is JS-only. No CSS file may be modified.
7. Scope: ONLY js/components/header.js, js/pages/portfolio.js, js/pages/about.js, js/pages/contacts.js may be modified.

THIS IS THE HIGHEST-RISK TASK IN THE PLAN for constraint 4. Verify it carefully and directly against the working tree, not just the diff.

Verify specifically:
- The three protected inline styles are still present and unmodified in js/pages/portfolio.js. Read the file and confirm each one, with line numbers.
- Trace the runtime code that depends on them: find `updateSlider` and the card click handler in js/pages/portfolio.js, and confirm the elements they mutate (`.before-img`, `.slider-handle`, `#portfolio-modal`) still resolve via the same querySelector calls after the class changes. A changed or dropped class on any of those elements would break the slider silently.
- `baCard.style.cursor = 'pointer';` is gone, and `.portfolio-ba-card` still carries both classes (`portfolio-card portfolio-ba-card`).
- The two previously class-less <span> elements in the preview halves now carry class="img-label", giving 4 total occurrences in the file.
- New class hooks added match the names the later CSS tasks will style: .lang-select, .portfolio-before-after-section, .portfolio-ba-title, .portfolio-ba-grid, .portfolio-ba-card, .card-images-preview, .preview-half, .img-label. Flag any name drift — a typo here silently produces unstyled elements three tasks later.
- All `${t.…}` expressions unchanged; all seven <option> lines unchanged; HTML comments (including the Russian-language section comments in portfolio.js) preserved.
- No CSS file touched; no file outside the four in scope touched.

ENVIRONMENT: no node, npm, or headless browser on this machine (python 3.14 only). Browser verification is legitimately impossible and should be reported as deferred, not as passed. Flag it if the implementer claimed a browser check passed.

Report:
- SPEC COMPLIANCE: ✅ or ❌, with specifics for anything missing or extra.
- TASK QUALITY: Approved, or a list of findings each labelled Critical / Important / Minor.
- Note any "⚠️ Cannot verify from diff" items separately.
Be concrete: cite file:line. Do not suggest improvements beyond the task's scope.

Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
